data.name: Dharvin
data.gender_notes: Dharvin is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dharma (Duty, Morality, Law) + Vin (God, Supreme Power) The name Dharvin signifies the foundation of the universe laid by God or the Supreme Power. The name Dharvin carries the meaning “Foundation of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharvin usually hope their child will grow to embody foundation of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Laying the foundation of righteous deeds
data.etymology: Dharvin belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Foundation of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharvin total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_sanskrit.name: धर्विन्
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Dharvin is derived from the Sanskrit word 'धर्वि' (dharvi), which means 'thunder' or 'sky'. The suffix 'न' (n) is added to form the masculine name 'धर्विन्' (dharvin). The name can also be interpreted as 'धर्मवान्' (dharma-van), meaning 'one who upholds dharma (righteousness)'. This name is also associated with abundance and prosperity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dharvin is derived from two Sanskrit roots - Dharma and Vin. In Hindu culture, Dharma represents moral duty, righteousness, and law. It is one of the Pillars of Hinduism. Having Dharma in a name reiterates the fundamental importance of following the path of righteousness and duty according to societal norms and societal obligations.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dharvin carries a profound spiritual significance. Vin in the name signifies God, the Supreme Power, or the Universal Consciousness. Combined with Dharma, the name represents the foundation of the universe laid by God, suggesting a close connection to the divine. Dharvin is a reminder of one's spiritual duty to uphold the principles of Dharma and strive for the continuous remembrance of, and connection to, the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dharvin: One who upholds righteousness and duty towards self and society, continually striving for moral growth and inner harmony. The name embodies the eternal quest for dharma (duty) in life.

historical_references.reference: Dharma was an important Indian king of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling from around 140 to 168 CE. The Satavahana empire flourished from around 230 BCE to 220 CE and was one of the major powers in ancient India during that time. Dharvin's name is possibly a variant of Dharma.

Another reference to the name Dharvin can be found in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, where a character named Dharvin is mentioned as a sage and a descendant of the great sage Vedavyasa. He played a significant role in the Mahabharata war by providing advice and guidance to the Pandava brothers.
